newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian oppn calls for race debate support.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian oppn calls for race debate support.

text.p: Australian Opposition Leader Kim Beazley asked the government on Monday to support a motion calling for a unified response to racial intolerance towards Aborigines and migrants.
"It (the motion) is intended to provide an opportunity for a bi-partisan endorsement of its contents," Beazley wrote in a letter to Prime Minister John Howard.
"Accordingly, it contains statements which are entirely consistent with both our parties' policies on these issues."
The motion follows controversial statements from independent politician Pauline Hanson during the past month.
Hanson's comments, attacking the government over the number of Asians in Australia and warning of an Asian invasion threat, sparked a widespread community response.
She has also said aboriginal welfare programmes were excessive and raised the spectre of civil war here if migrants and Aborigines continued to get special treatment.

The motion, which Beazley proposes to move unless the government decides to take it over, supports Governor-General Sir William Deane's recent comments that Aborigines needed assistance from the goverment.
Howard has been criticised for not making a stronger stand against Hanson, although he has spoken out broadly against intolerance and non-discriminatory immigration.
Earlier on Monday, he denied Australia was in the throes of a racial debate, accusing the media of inflaming the issue.
